directive.quote: Fix the cause in its owner: frames never run once their deadline has passed (the frame carries its deadline, and the Mac drops expired ones); remove whatever makes a principal check take seconds; the principal check should take well under 1 s end to end. No timeout bumps as the fix.

preserve: a session is admitted, acknowledged once and bound to its exact route, lifetime and registration
the registration is read before a message's bytes leave, and a refused registration retires the session
a lost or late reply retires the session and is an unknown outcome, never resent
the Mac serves only messages of its own route while its acknowledged session lasts
allowed_deltas: readiness is judged on local facts (acknowledged, retired, lifetime) without the stream lock or the registration owner
the registration is read once per message, at the send boundary, and again only where a check releases a result
a message the connection never sends is answered with a correlated refusal, and the Mac answers a message whose deadline passed before dispatch with a refusal and never dispatches it
one stderr line per message on the Mac: the operation's name, queued and run times, deadline left and outcome
banned_substitutions: a longer timeout or deadline in place of removing the wait
a cached registration answer in place of reading it where a credential leaves
a request key, credential, input or reply in a log line
